name: weather-flood
description: Set heavy rain weather, drill holes that flood, and verify water-sensitive explosive fails to detonate

steps.description: Left unmarked: no UI sets weather at all -- grepping src/ui for gameConsole?.(`weather finds zero call sites. This is a real gap, not a conversion shortfall: nothing lets a player change the weather, only `weather set` from the console/scenario harness. Also fixed a scenario bug while here: the command was `weather heavy_rain` (missing `set`), which mining.ts's weatherCommand silently falls through to a plain read for -- the flood test never actually set heavy_rain at all. Corrected to `weather set heavy_rain`.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat, no employees exist yet to pay

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15
steps.description: Corrected from rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 4 holes): the click drags the (15,15)-(20,20) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = round(5/3)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json and repeated in several other files this batch (hauling-gate.json, safety-projection-visual.json, core-loop-visual.json). Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged.

boomite is waterSensitive:true (ExplosiveCatalog.ts); every hole here is flooded (raining, no tubing installed -- WetHoles.ts's wetHoles()) so this blast now genuinely detonates weak (Finding #39: BlastExecution.ts never wired the water/flood mechanic into the real energy calculation at all -- waterEffect/wetHoles existed but had zero effect on any blast until this fix). No state field exposes the blast report's clearedVoxels/rating directly, so the weakening itself is proven by dedicated tests rather than a scenario assertion: a direct trace of this exact command sequence shows 27 cleared voxels / $83,500 ore value flooded vs. 395 cleared voxels / $1,337,550 dry (~14x weaker, same seed/grid/charge) -- confirmed end-to-end through the real console command pipeline by tests/integration/weather-blast.integration.test.ts, and at the physics level by new tests in BlastCalc.test.ts/BlastExecution.test.ts.
